{{nihongo|'''Musanimasu Shrine'''|牟佐坐神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

=== History ===
=== Foundation ===
The origin is said to be enshrinement of Ikazuchi-no-Kami by the immigrant leader Misa no Suguri Ao in the era of {{ill|Emperor Ankō|ar|الإمبراطور أنكو|arz|الامبراطور انكو|azb|آنکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Ankō|cs|Ankó|de|Ankō|es|Ankō Tennō|fa|امپراتور آنکو|fr|Ankō (empereur)|hr|Ankō|hu|Ankó japán császár|id|Kaisar Ankō|it|Ankō (imperatore del Giappone)|ja|安康天皇|ka|ანკო|ko|안코 천황|nl|Anko (keizer)|pl|Ankō|pt|Anko|ru|Император Анко|sh|Car Ankō|simple|Emperor Ankō|sl|Cesar Anko|sv|Anko|th|จักรพรรดิอังโก|tl|Emperador Ankō|tr|Ankō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Анко|uz|Imperator Ankō|vi|Thiên hoàng Ankō|yo|Emperor Ankō|zh|安康天皇|zh_min_nan|Ankô Thian-hông|zh_yue|安康天皇|qid=Q361010}}. Misa (=Musa) was a place name in Takachi District, {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}, regarded as the base area of the {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|Q10870550|qid=Q10870550}} who naturalized under {{ill|Achi no Omi|Q11657596|qid=Q11657596}}. Misa no Suguri Ao was a favored retainer of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}}, one of the {{ill|Five kings of Wa|Q1152880|qid=Q1152880}}. ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'' records missions he led to Wu/Song in Yūryaku 8 ({{ill|464|Q30150|qid=Q30150}}) and Yūryaku 12 ({{ill|468|Q30823|qid=Q30823}}), though these are not found in the ''{{ill|Book of Song|Q1143142|qid=Q1143142}}''.

=== Historical outline ===
According to ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'', during the {{ill|Jinshin War|Q2378252|qid=Q2378252}}, in Takachi District, the deity “Kotoshironushi at {{ill|Kawamata Shrine (Q11553360)|Q11553360|qid=Q11553360|lt=Takachi Shrine}} and Ikudama-no-Kami at Misa Shrine” possessed {{ill|Takechi no Kome|Q11669864|qid=Q11669864|lt=Takachi Agatanushi Kome}} and gave an {{ill|Oracle|Q217123|qid=Q217123}}: “Offer horses and various weapons at the tomb of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188|lt=Kamuyamato Iwarehiko}},” and then Prince Ōama (later {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ar|الإمبراطور تيمو|arz|الامبراطور تيمو|azb|تمو|ca|Tenmu|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر تێنمو|cs|Temmu|de|Temmu|eo|Temmu|es|Tenmu Tennō|fa|امپراتور تنمو|fr|Tenmu|hak|Tenmu Thiên-fòng|he|טמו, קיסר יפן|hu|Tenmu japán császár|id|Kaisar Tenmu|it|Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|ka|ტენმუ|ko|덴무 천황|nl|Tenmu|pl|Tenmu|pt|Tenmu|ru|Император Тэмму|sh|Car Temmu|simple|Emperor Tenmu|sl|Cesar Tenmu|su|Kaisar Temmu|sv|Tenmu|th|จักรพรรดิเท็มมุ|tl|Emperador Temmu|tr|Temmu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Темму|vi|Thiên hoàng Tenmu|yo|Emperor Temmu|zh|天武天皇|zh_min_nan|Tenmu Thian-hông|zh_yue|天武天皇|qid=Q335181}}) would be protected.<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', vol. 28</ref> After his enthronement, divine rank was granted to Misa-ni-masu Ikudama-no-Kami for the first time in history. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it is listed as a great shrine and recorded as receiving offerings for monthly and Niiname rites.<br/>Its former rank was listed as {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Court rank ===
* {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} 3 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), {{ill|January 27|Q2284|qid=Q2284}}: promoted from Junior Fifth Lower to Junior Fifth Upper (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'') - written as “Musanimasu-no-Kami.”

=== Access ===
* Just west on foot from {{ill|Okadera Station|Q7081721|qid=Q7081721}} on the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yoshino Line}} of {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085}}.
